demo.prompt: Research the principles of empty states in web app interfaces: what makes a good one, what makes a bad one, and what people struggle with. Quick depth is enough.
demo.result:
A brief of 29 claims from 17 sources, each claim ending in its source numbers and a confidence label. Its header and two entries:

*Researched: 2026-11-18 · Depth: quick · Mode: subagents · 17 sources*

**Method:** three researcher agents, one per facet, then three separate auditor agents that saw only each claim, its quote and its URLs and fetched every cited page again. 30 claims were recorded; 29 were audited confirmed and 1 weak. Claims dropped by the audit: 0.

- **Empty states come in types by cause, and each type needs different content.** Carbon groups them into three, "Basic empty states for first use, user action confirmation, and error management", with a goal for each. [2][4] (established)
- **"Empty" is decided from the row count alone, so the empty state renders while data is still loading.** A bug report on a React table library says the table body "only checks for empty rows (!rows.length) but doesn't consider the isLoading state". [9][10] (supported)

It also lists what it could not cover: design systems whose pages would not load, and that each pain point rests on a single report.
demo.caption: Real output, shortened. The run took about 12 minutes and used 6 subagents.

before.label: Same request, no skill
before.text:
- 27 claims from 9 sources, in about 5 minutes with one agent.
- 8 of 8 sampled quotes were found on the cited page.
- The agent checked its own quotes. Two sources could only be paraphrased and are marked as such.
- Says its "struggles" section is the weakest: it comes from what the sources warn about, with no community reports.
- Sources are named in the text, with no numbered citations.
before.note: Already careful work: it dropped 8 claims it could not trace to a page it had read, and said so.

after.label: With principle-research
after.text:
- 29 claims from 17 sources, in about 12 minutes with 6 subagents.
- 8 of 8 sampled quotes were found on the cited page.
- Separate auditor agents re-fetched every citation and gave each claim a verdict: 29 confirmed, 1 weak.
- Pain points come from real reports: GitHub issues, Hacker News and UX Stack Exchange threads.
- Every claim has numbered sources and a confidence label, and the method and gaps are stated.
after.note: Citation accuracy was the same in this test. The skill added breadth, an independent audit and a traceable format, for more than twice the time.

method: One run each, same request, same model (Claude Fable 5.2) and same tools, November 2026; the only difference was the skill folder. A third agent then re-fetched the first 8 quoted claims of each brief and checked the quotes against the pages.
